stdout: usage: bale apply [-h] [--staging-dir STAGING_DIR] [--show-validator]
[--show-apply-script] [--dry-run] [--verbose]
[--no-interact] [--allow-out-of-scope PATH]
[--allow-missing-required-check NAME]
[--accept-checkpoint-change] [--accept-base-drift PATH]
[--no-sandbox] [--json]
[tarball]
Validate and apply a response tarball: pre-flight the manifest and its gates,
overlay files/ and run apply.sh in staging, run the planner's blind checkpoint
(when [validation] base is configured) and the response's validation.sh,
commit the session to bale/<sid>, and walk the verdict — PASS merges into the
origin branch by default; HOLD keeps bale/<sid> and the staging copy for
inspection and names the two next steps, `bale retry <new-tarball>` or `bale
revert <sid>` (a HOLD whose cause is the checkpoint itself goes through `bale
amend-checkpoint` first). A bailout response prints the `bale handoff` next
step and closes the session; a clarification response records its questions as
a round of the session's exchange thread and keeps the session open for `bale
relay`.
The tarball argument is resolved against apply.search_paths in bale.toml when
set: relative names are tried against cwd first, then each configured
directory in order, first match wins. Absolute paths bypass search. Configure
via `bale config init`.
The tarball argument may be omitted entirely (bare `bale apply`, v0.4.16;
widened v0.4.29; bounded v0.4.32): bale lists the response-*.tar.gz files in
cwd and each apply.search_paths directory, opens only the two newest by
modification time, and resolves the newest of those whose manifest answers any
open session — an exact tie refuses — then echoes the resolved identity (path,
the session it answers and the open set, sha256, mtime) and asks y/N before
applying — decline is the default, and piped stdin declines without a prompt.
Every non-resolving outcome (no candidate among the examined files, an exact
modification-time tie, no open session, non-interactive stdin) refuses with a
remedy rather than guessing, and the no-candidate refusal names each examined
file with why it was rejected; files not named response-*.tar.gz are never
candidates and are never opened.
Inspection flags (--show-validator, --show-apply-script, --dry-run) look
without applying: the first two print a script from the tarball and need no
open session (and therefore require the tarball named — they don't compose
with the bare form); --dry-run runs the read-only validation half against the
open session and prints the plan, touching neither the worktree nor git.
positional arguments:
tarball               Path to response-<sid>.tar.gz. Omit it (bare `bale
apply`) to resolve the newest response tarball
answering an open session across cwd and
apply.search_paths, with an identity echo and a
decline-default y/N before anything applies; ambiguity
refuses loudly rather than guessing.
options:
-h, --help            show this help message and exit
--staging-dir STAGING_DIR
Where to stage the apply (default:
<repo>/.bale/staging/<sid>, per open session). An
explicit path is resolved relative to cwd, is used
verbatim (no <sid> suffix), and is refused if it
already exists.
--show-validator      Print the tarball's validation.sh and exit, without
applying. Resolves the tarball through
apply.search_paths like a real apply but needs no open
session and no clean working tree. Combine with
--show-apply-script to print both.
--show-apply-script   Print the tarball's apply.sh and exit, without
applying. Same no-session, no-clean-tree semantics as
--show-validator; when both are given, apply.sh prints
first.
--dry-run             Validate the tarball against the open session and
print what apply would do (the change set and the
checks validation.sh would run), then stop. Requires
an open session (for the responds_to check) but no
clean working tree: no branch is created, nothing is
staged into the worktree, nothing is committed.
--verbose             Stream validation.sh output live to the terminal in
addition to the session log (BALE.md §8.5). Without
it, validation output goes to .bale/logs/<sid>.log
only and the walkthrough summary carries the verdict.
No effect with --dry-run, which does not run
validation.sh.
--no-interact         Run without prompting (BALE.md §5.4/§8.7): the
walkthrough takes its default action (merge on PASS;
hold for inspection on HOLD, exiting non-zero) and the
post-apply hook confirmation resolves from
apply.hook_auto_accept in bale.toml (unset/false =
decline). Every bypassed prompt logs the decision
taken and its source to the terminal and the session
log. The mode can also be enabled per config via
apply.no_interact = true; run `bale config init`.
--allow-out-of-scope PATH
Admit one changes[] path that lies outside the
session's own declared scope, past the own-scope drift
gate (BALE.md §8.1 step 14, §11 row 22). Repeat the
flag per path; any out-of-scope path NOT named still
refuses. Per-invocation only — there is deliberately
no config key. Every use is logged prominently (FORCE:
line in the session log) and the admitted paths are
stamped into the session's telemetry record. On a TTY
the refusal also offers the same admission as a per-
path y/N (default decline; v0.4.27) — the typed flag
is the non-interactive form, and every refusal prints
a composed re-run line carrying one flag per drifted
path.
--allow-missing-required-check NAME
Admit one required check name past the required-check
superset gate (BALE.md §8.1 step 15, §11 row 26)
despite its absence from the manifest's
validation_will_run. Repeat the flag per name; any
missing required name NOT named still refuses. Per-
invocation only — there is deliberately no config key,
per the ratified override contract (a standing opt-out
is the rejected self-oracle-adjacent silent bypass).
Every effective use is logged prominently (FORCE: line
in the session log) and the admitted names are stamped
into the session's telemetry record.
--accept-checkpoint-change
Accept a blind checkpoint that changed between pack
and apply (v0.3.28, board 6 session C; BALE.md §8.5):
the request's pack-time provenance stamp no longer
matches the base-tree bytes about to run, and without
this flag apply refuses — the oracle changed, a
legitimate planner edit or interference, and either is
worth stopping for. With it, apply executes the
CURRENT base-tree version — the planner's latest
committed oracle, never the stale stamped bytes — logs
a FORCE: line, and records stamp_matched: false in the
attempt's telemetry stamp. Per-invocation only —
deliberately no config key, per the ratified override
contract.
--accept-base-drift PATH
Admit one changes[] path past the base-drift gate
(BALE.md §8.1 step 17, §11 row 36) despite its base-
tree bytes no longer matching the request's pack-time
provenance.base_files stamp — the base moved between
pack and apply, and the whole-file overlay would
revert the intervening edits (the lost-update hazard
the gate exists for). Admitting a path lands the
response's bytes OVER the moved base, deliberately
superseding those edits. Repeat the flag per path —
mirroring --allow-out-of-scope's grammar; any drifted
path NOT named still refuses. Per-invocation only —
deliberately no config key, per the ratified override
contract. Every effective use is logged prominently
(FORCE: line in the session log) and the admitted
paths are stamped into the attempt's
base_drift_overrides telemetry field.
--no-sandbox          Run the response scripts (apply.sh, the blind
checkpoint, validation.sh) UNCONFINED for this
invocation — no namespace sandbox, operator
privileges, inherited environment, network on (v0.4.4,
ADR-0016; BALE.md §8.5). The sandbox is default-on for
every apply; this escape exists for debugging the
sandbox itself, not for routine convenience. Per-
invocation only, and every use is logged prominently
(FORCE: line in the session log) and stamped
sandbox_escaped: true into the attempt's telemetry
record (v0.4.5, board 10 S2; BALE.md §8.9). For hosts
without unprivileged user namespaces the durable form
is bale.toml's project-layer [sandbox] enabled = false
(v0.4.26, board 75): same unconfined semantics, FORCE-
logged naming the key on every run, stamped
sandbox_confined: false / sandbox_off_source: config;
this flag is redundant beside it. On a TTY, a host
where the sandbox self-probe refuses offers the same
escape as a y/N (default decline, FORCE-logged,
sandbox_off_source: prompt; v0.4.27) — this flag is
the non-interactive form, and the refusal prints a
composed re-run line carrying it.
--json                Emit the end-of-run apply report as one line of JSON
on stdout. Keys are a stable contract for downstream
tooling: outcome
(applied|held|reverted|bailout|clarification|dry-
run|scope-drift-refused|required-check-refused|base-
drift-refused), sid, log, verdict (validation.sh
state/exit_code/claims; null when it did not run),
merge (walkthrough action/merged/tag/origin_branch;
null when no walkthrough ran), drift (the own-scope
refusal detail; null otherwise), required_checks (the
required-check refusal detail; null otherwise),
base_drift (the base-drift refusal detail; null
otherwise). Stream discipline: '[bale] ' lines,
prompts, and the human banners go to stderr; stdout
carries exactly the JSON line on the reporting paths —
exit 0, plus the held/reverted/scope-drift-
refused/required-check-refused/base-drift-refused
exit-1 outcomes. Error paths exit through stderr with
nothing on stdout. Pair with --no-interact for
scripted runs. No effect with --show-validator/--show-
apply-script, whose whole output is a script body on
stdout.
